pr_title: fs: fcb: add option to disable CRC for fcb entries
pr_body:
Add option to disable CRC for fcb entries. This improves the write throughput significantly at the cost of not detecting corrupted data in flash. This is beneficial for aplications that needs the extra write throughput, where error detection is done elsewhere.

Fixes #53707

Signed-off-by: Eivind Jølsgard <eivind.jolsgard@nordicsemi.no>
pr_comments: I agree that the option should enable the CRC, and be on by default.

Thank you for your feedback! 
> It would be better to provide a config option that enables the crc check (set default to yes, CONFIG_FCB_ENDMARKER_CRC8)

The reason for doing it like this is to make it possible to have FCBs with CRC check enabled and disabled in the same application. Having a Kconfig that enable/disable CRC will apply for all FCBs in the application, but maybe that is ok? I agree that the Kconfig option, as it is per now, can be a bit confusing. Maybe it is ok to drop the Kconfig option and only rely on the flag in `struct fcb`, as not setting the flag would give the original behavior?

> And it would be good that the solution would also work for existing fcb areas on devices: 
When writing either write the CRC8 or FIXED_END_MARKER depending on the config,
When reading accept CRC8 or CRC8/FIXED_END_MARKER depending on the config

Good point! Existing solutions will still work with CRC enabled, but I can rewrite this so that existing solutions can disable CRC if they find it beneficial.

> The reason for doing it like this is to make it possible to have FCBs with CRC check enabled and disabled in the same application. Having a Kconfig that enable/disable CRC will apply for all FCBs in the application

What I think should happen is that when nobody is interested in disabling CRC then it should be possible to not add the feature.
If somebody is interested, then it should be available, and CRC should be Y be default, but you should be able to disable it for a specific  FCB instance, is you use more than one.

> > The reason for doing it like this is to make it possible to have FCBs with CRC check enabled and disabled in the same application. Having a Kconfig that enable/disable CRC will apply for all FCBs in the application
> 
> What I think should happen is that when nobody is interested in disabling CRC then it should be possible to not add the feature. If somebody is interested, then it should be available, and CRC should be Y be default, but you should be able to disable it for a specific FCB instance, is you use more than one.

~Ok, I added a Kconfig option, `CONFIG_FCB_FORCE_ENDMARKER_CRC8` that is enabled by default. Name is up for discussion, but I think that should make it clear enough that disabling it still give the possibility to enable CRC if desired.~

Update: Replaced with `CONFIG_FCB_ALLOW_TO_DISABLE_ENDMARKER_CRC` after discussion with @de-nordic.

> > The reason for doing it like this is to make it possible to have FCBs with CRC check enabled and disabled in the same application. Having a Kconfig that enable/disable CRC will apply for all FCBs in the application
> 
> What I think should happen is that when nobody is interested in disabling CRC then it should be possible to not add the feature. If somebody is interested, then it should be available, and CRC should be Y be default, but you should be able to disable it for a specific FCB instance, is you use more than one.

I guess this rules out a CONFIG option.

> 
> I guess this rules out a CONFIG option.

Wait, I am little lost. We are going to have CONFIG, the Kconfig?

> > I guess this rules out a CONFIG option.
> 
> Wait, I am little lost. We are going to have CONFIG, the Kconfig?

What I meant is having a Kconfig option (a `CONFIG_...`) does not play well with a per instance option.
Decided to keep the Kconfig as `CONFIG_FCB_ALLOW_TO_DISABLE_ENDMARKER_CRC` after discussion with @de-nordic.

@eivindj-nordic, things that I don't like and need fixing:

a. CONFIG option name, this should be something like `CONFIG_FCB_ALLOW_FIXED_ENDMARKER`,
b. The endmarker should not be `CRC8_CCITT_INITIAL_VALUE`,
c. The swap from `fcb_elem_get_info`: checking a crc to `fcb_elem_get_info` generating a end marker, this is confusing for users that have studied the code in the past,
d. It would be better to use `IS_ENABLED()` instead of `#if defined`,

The solution should be a lot simpler:
`fcb_elem_crc8` is split up in `fcb_elem_crc8()` (does only the calculation) and `fcb_elem_endmarker()` (does checking and sets fixed marker or calls `fcb_elem_crc8()` to set the marker.
`fcb_elem_info` uses `fcb_elem_endmarker()` instead of `fcb_elem_crc8` and compares, if it fails (and the fixed marker is enabled) it calls `fcb_elem_crc8()` and recompares

@eivindj-nordic, if I made no mistake the code size with the option disabled (standard) should result in exactly the same code as before inserting the option. And the crc calculation will only be repeated twice in the case of a bad crc and the option fixed marker option disabled for a fcb instance while it is globally enabled.

> @eivindj-nordic, if I made no mistake the code size with the option disabled (standard) should result in exactly the same code as before inserting the option. 

@Laczen After addressing your comments, I observe an increase of 4 bytes of flash for my test-application. The FCB flags has to be added to the FCB struct always for 
` if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_FCB_ALLOW_FIXED_ENDMARKER) && (_fcb->f_flags & FCB_FLAGS_CRC_DISABLED)) {`.
 I think that is ok.  

> And the crc calculation will only be repeated twice in the case of a bad crc and the option fixed marker option disabled for a fcb instance while it is globally enabled.

Yes, there will be some additional processing when CONFIG_FCB_ALLOW_FIXED_ENDMARKER is enabled, and CRC is enabled for the specific FCB. However, it only has to read a couple of bytes extra in that case and not the entire entry content, as is done in` fcb_elem_crc8`. I think that is acceptable when `CONFIG_FCB_ALLOW_FIXED_ENDMARKER` is enabled.

> > @eivindj-nordic, if I made no mistake the code size with the option disabled (standard) should result in exactly the same code as before inserting the option.
> 
> @Laczen After addressing your comments, I observe an increase of 4 bytes of flash for my test-application. The FCB flags has to be added to the FCB struct always for ` if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_FCB_ALLOW_FIXED_ENDMARKER) && (_fcb->f_flags & FCB_FLAGS_CRC_DISABLED)) {`. I think that is ok.
> 
It should be possible not to have this (maybe by splitting this into two if's). I thought the compiler was smarter 😀

> A small nitpick, with seperate crc8/fixed em calculation the if from line 29 (original fcb_elem_info.c) would better be repeated in each separate calculation.

Updated. Thank you for your patience :)

issue_context.title: fs: fcb: Add option to disable CRC for FCB entries
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
The `fcb_append_finish()` takes a long time to process as it is reading back the content written to flash to calculate the CRC for the FCB entry. This severely impacts the throughput when writing to the FCB. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
For some applications, the CRC check is not needed, for instance if this is done at a higher level, or there are other mechanisms for error detection in place. Disabling the CRC, hereby removing the need to read back the written content in `fcb_append_finish()`, has shown to improve the write throughput significantly for my application, increasing the write throughput by around 75% (675 kb/s -> 1180 kb/s).  

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
An alternative solution could be to calculate the CRC when writing the content to flash. This would remove the need to read back the content in `crc_append_finish()`, but would still spend resources computing the CRC. The FCB does not have a function for writing content data, but is instead relying on e.g. `flash_area_write()` for this.  The API would therefore need to change for this, e.g. by adding a dedicated `fcb_content_write()` function that can calculate the CRC while writing to flash. As a  side note, this would also enable error checking in the write-phase, if the underlying write driver does not support it, as the pre-calculated CRC can be compared with calculating the CRC of the flash content. This change would require more work, API changes, and it would also does not increase the write throughput as much as the proposed solution (a solution calculating the CRC based on the written data resulted in a write throughput of 1080 kb/s). Therefore it is left as a suggestion for further improvements to the FCB.

**Additional context**
None

review_comments: In `fcb_elem_crc8()` this is then no longer required.
true, I kept it as `fcb_elem_crc8` is called other places as well (`fcb_elem_info`), but here it is guarded by calling `fcb_elem_endmarker` first anyway. Will update :)
